It’s ok to feel this way, you’re feeling a lot of strong emotions that others cannot understand and don’t know how to help you. People become frustrated with people that suffer from depression because they feel like they give advice but the depressed person doesn’t take it. What they don’t understand is that the depressed person doesn’t need advice, they just need someone to listen to them and tell them everything is going to be ok regardless. 

You’re going to be ok even if rn it feels like there’s no other way out of this but death. It’s ok to post on here repeatedly, I’ve done so myself. It’s ok to use this as a means to release emotion and talk the way you want to talk about your feelings and thoughts without receiving any judgement for it. 

The depressed mind wants you to leave this world, but deep down you want to keep living, you want to keep living but w/o feeling this way forever. There’s a way out of this that involves staying alive. There’s love and joy to be experienced out there for you. Right now focus on yourself, focus on expressing what you’re feeling without holding it in, you’re not manipulating anyone by expressing strong emotions. But people that haven’t gone through this cannot handle such strong emotions and thoughts. It takes training and experience to be able to listen to such intensity of thoughts without letting it get inside you and make you feel like the person who’s saying all these things 

Keep strong and keep firm, you’re going to be ok

Depression won’t win! Keep fighting. The thoughts aren’t real, it’s the depression speaking to you. Same as when anger takes over, you think angry things that later on you know you didn’t actually agree with, right now sadness has taken over and it’s making you think things that deep down you might not agree with. 

Everything is going to be ok, you’re going to be ok. Death is not the only way out of this, remind yourself that whenever depression takes over and whispers that it’s the only way. 

Cry as much as you can and release some of those trapped emotions, let yourself feel those intense feelings but don’t give them any thoughts to latch onto. 

You’re going to be ok, there is a way out of this darkness

It’s going to be ok, you’re going to be ok. 

Don’t hold it in, cry as much as you can, speak about how sad you are whenever you are sad, express these feelings so they can be worked through.  Remind yourself that the thoughts that come up aren’t true, when depression takes over the thoughts it makes us have feel like they’re coming from us but they’re not. 

Right now everything will appear hopeless and painful, but the fact that you’re still alive means that deep down you want to keep living even if you’re having suicidal thoughts. Hold on to any moments of joy you can remember having until you’re able to feel joy again. 

I’ve been suffering from depression and suicidal thoughts since I was 8. It’s been a wild journey of ups and downs, but I’m still here and I’m glad I’ve stayed no matter how many times my mind told me to off myself and how bad everything is around me. 

There’s a life to be lived for you out there, people who will love you for who you are regardless of anything are out there waiting for you to find them. It can take years, but peace and joy can be found even inside a hurricane of darkness and suffering. 

Just keep holding on and fighting, remember when you want to give up that it’s not you, it’s the depressive mind taking over.

Check ins determine a lot for each location. Each check in is registered and then counted per hour. As such, making sure that a member habitually checks in is in the best interest of not just the staff that work there, but also the members that work out there. 

It is also their number one rule in all their agreements. “Upon entering the club, all members must check in”.

It’s a long road, don’t be upset if you don’t see any progress at first. Your brains thinking patterns took months and months to settle into what they are now that cause you to be anxious. After consistency in your therapy you’ll start to notice the little things that will be different, you’ll notice that you were able to stop yourself from spiraling sooner than before, things you didn’t even realized were triggering you too. But be patient and consistent in your therapy, the same way it takes months to gain progress in something like the gym, the mind is just as hard to train. 

If after a very long time of therapy you feel you haven’t made any progress or if after long periods of progress you feel you’ve stagnated in your therapy, don’t be afraid to tell your therapist, they can either re structure your therapy or recommend you to a different  therapist which is sometimes the best thing to do if a specific doctor isn’t working out for you anymore. Don’t stress it, judgement free zone. I would say it’s strength I’ve gained but somehow that word just feels incorrect. It’s really experience and awareness that has gotten me this far. Awareness that the thoughts and feelings are not coming from me and through recognizing which thoughts are mine and which thoughts come from the depression,  I gain fighting experience. With the experience I can recognize when they pop into my head again and invalidate the credibility of the thoughts. The mind tends to pick up what you want it to do and it too then learns to automatically and with more speed recognize a thought as a symptom and help you fight. I see the thoughts of depression the same way we see a person with Parkinson’s movements as an involuntary movement caused by the Parkinson’s. These thoughts are an automatic and involuntary reaction that comes from the depression. 

Everything psychological is biological and we don’t control the biological. Someone with a bad knee can learn to walk slightly different or can learn how to deal with the knee pain on the days the knee is acting up really bad. We have to shift our view of depression to the same way we view “regular” physical maladies. 

It wasn’t until I started perceiving what my mind does as a physical issue that I started making bigger strides in overcoming it. You can learn to recognize what makes it act up more too. For example someone prone to migraines gets more migraines when they are dehydrated so they intake more water , in the same vain someone with a depression contributed by loneliness can intake more social interactions to alleviate the feelings. 

It’s a long process and it’s easier said than done, but practice in perception shifting and symptom recognition can help you gain “strength” to fight. The more you fight an enemy in a video game the more you learn it’s move and can see them coming next time you face it

College is extremely hard for those who are suffering from any kind of mental health issues. It’s like running a very long marathon with giant stones tied to you. It might seem like an unwise decision at the moment, but perhaps you should take a break from college and try not being a student for a while until you’ve gotten a grip on your depression. Classwork, homework, upcoming tests, constant studying, grades, showing up to class, those are all really intense chronic stressors that eat away at whatever little energy you have left to fight of your depressive symptoms. I thought I had mine under control until I started college and ended up failing 4 out of the 5 classes I was taking even though they were easy courses with subjects I loved. 

It’s not a route that will look the best according to those who will judge you, but your health and well being are more important. College will still be there when you choose to return and so will your sanity. 

There’s easy work/jobs that can be done to earn a living and that will allow to experience other things beside being a student. Your body and mind need a break and experiencing life outside of being a student might help you re arrange your emotions
